title: From Ukraine to Iran, Attacks on Civilian Sites Put Us All at Risk
gist: A CNAS commentary (excerpt, originally in Inkstick) warns that across recent conflicts—Ukraine-Russia, the US-Israeli war on Iran, Israel's Lebanon strikes and Sudan's civil war—attacks on civilian infrastructure that do not meet legitimate-military-target criteria are becoming brazenly normalized, eroding the norm against them and paving the way for further escalation, with the UN warning of clear violations of international humanitarian law.

insights.claim: Recent conflicts show a trend of increasingly brazen violations of the foundational norms of armed conflict, with a rise in attacks on civilian infrastructure that do not meet the criteria for legitimate military targets.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Norm erosion around civilian-infrastructure targeting raises the ceiling on future escalation—a structural risk premium for regions exposed to these conflicts.
insights.quote: there has been a trend of increasingly brazen violations of the foundational norms of armed conflict
insights.locator: The last several years have seen military conflict fan out

insights.claim: CNAS argues continued attacks on civilian infrastructure—exemplified by recent Ukrainian strikes on Russia's Wildberries e-commerce warehouses—will further erode the norm and may lead Russia to abandon any restraint it still retains.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: If Russia sheds remaining restraint, escalation risk in the Ukraine war rises materially—watch commercial/logistics infrastructure as new targets.
insights.quote: the power of the norm against them will only erode further, paving the way for more and more escalatory actions
insights.locator: If this trend of attacks on civilian infrastructure continues

insights.claim: This year US-Israeli strikes have hit civilian sites in Iran, Israeli bombings in Lebanon have targeted roads, bridges and hospitals that Israel dubiously calls military sites, and both sides in Sudan's war have targeted schools, medical facilities, dams and displacement camps.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: The spread of civilian targeting across three theaters signals a systemic breakdown in restraint norms, not isolated incidents—broadening humanitarian and reputational risk.
insights.quote: US-Israeli strikes have hit a slate of civilian sites in Iran, while Israeli bombings in Lebanon have targeted roads, bridges, and hospitals

insights.claim: The UN's Stéphane Dujarric called for an end to 'attacks against civilians and civilian infrastructure,' describing them as a clear violation of international humanitarian law wherever they occur.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Explicit UN condemnation frames the legal and diplomatic exposure for states pursuing such strikes—a factor in sanctions and coalition dynamics.
insights.quote: a clear violation of international humanitarian law, wherever they occur
